title: Speculating and making deductions / Especular y ak jëngu jënd-dëkk
bridge: In Wolof, we use 'dëgg naa' or 'dëgguma' to speculate. In English, we use modals like 'must', 'might', 'could', 'can't' + infinitive. The key is that 'must' expresses a very strong deduction (positive) and 'can't' a strong negation; 'might', 'may', and 'could' express possibility. Be careful: do not use 'must not' to deduce the opposite, because in English 'must not' means prohibition.
rule: To make deductions in the present in English, we use the following modals followed by the base form of the verb: 'must' (strong deduction that something is true), 'can't' (strong deduction that something is false), 'might', 'may', 'could' (possibility, less certain). To talk about the past, we use 'must have + past participle', 'can't have + past participle', 'might have + past participle', etc. The structure is: subject + modal + base verb (present) or modal + have + past participle (past). Tip: In Wolof, 'dëgg naa' and 'dëgguma' are equivalent, but in English, you do not say 'must not be' to deduce the opposite; use 'can't be'.

concept_examples.translation: He must be tired after the long trip.

concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ maɪt hæv fərˈɡɒtən ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ/

common_error.explanation: The error occurs because in Wolof, we say 'dëgguma' to express negative deduction, but in English, 'must not' expresses prohibition ('must not' = no permission). To deduce that something is impossible or false, use 'can't' (or 'couldn't' for more formality). The alternative 'must be out' is valid because the meaning is equivalent: deducing that someone is not at home.

examples.note: We use 'must' when we are almost certain about something because there is evidence. In Wolof, 'dëgg naa'.

title: Expressing regret and hypothetical situations / Expresar arrepentimiento e hipótesis
bridge: Xaleyi ci yoon wi, yu bees ci kondoom ak subjonctif ba noppi xaleyi ci arrepentimiento (naata ci waa 'si tuviera tiempo, iría'). Xaleyi, la structure mën a def ci passé simple (u passé parfait) ci clause 'if' ak 'would' + verbe ci clause principale. Li mbirum yu bees ci 'si tendría', 'if I would have' laa def ci yoon wi, waaye ci yoon wi clause 'if' mënul a jëf 'would'. Ci benn xaleyi, ci yoon wi passé parfait ('had + participle') laa def ci lieu ci condicional composé.
rule: Ci yoon wi B1, ba noppi xaleyi ci yoon wi jëf ci passé (segundo condicional), yu bees 'if + passé simple' (u 'if + passé continu') ci clause condicional, ak 'would + forme base' ci clause principale. Exemples: 'If I had more time, I would travel.' (Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría). Note ba 'were' laa jëf ci yoon wi ci 'if I were' (waaye 'was' laa jëf ci yoon wi anglais informal). Ba noppi xaleyi ci passé (tercer condicional), yu bees 'if + passé parfait' (had + participle) ak 'would have + participle' ci principale: 'If I had studied, I would have passed.' (Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado). Lu bees, yu bees 'I wish' + passé parfait ba noppi xaleyi: 'I wish I had studied.' (Ojalá hubiera estudiado). Jëf ci clause 'if' mënul a jëf 'would' u 'will'. Ci yoon wi formel, 'were' laa jëf: 'If he were here...'.

title: Discussing Advantages and Disadvantages / Waxtaanee xeexu ak xeexu
bridge: Ci waxu ñuul solemes usar 'xeexu' ak 'xeexu' waxeewu, dafay waxu ingeel solemes usar 'advantages' ak 'disadvantages' rekk, ngir verb yu bari 'have' ak 'there are'. Waxuña, ci ingeel, waxu ñuul solemes usar 'pros and cons' ci waxtu yu mel ni, moom ci waxu ñuul solemes waxe ngir wuññi ci waxu spañol. Jëfandikukat bu njëkk ci ñuul solemes waxe 'por un lado' 'for one side' – waxu ngi ci wax ñuul solemes waxe 'on the one hand'.
rule:
Ñuul solemes waxtaanee xeexu ak xeexu ci ingeel ci B1, jëfandikukat bii waxe:
1. 'One advantage (of) is that...' / 'One disadvantage (of) is that...' – ñuul solemes waxe ci waxe ngir suufu ak verb.
2. 'The advantages of + noun/gerund are...' ngir ñuul solemes waxe.
3. 'On the one hand... on the other hand...' ngir waxtaanee bii xeexu.
4. 'However' ak 'Nevertheless' ngir ñuul solemes waxe ci xeexu.
5. 'Pros and cons' moom ci waxu ngi ci waxe ngir wuññi, waxu ñuul solemes waxe 'Let's weigh the pros and cons.'
Jëfandikukat bu njëkk ci ingeel, ñuul solemes waxe 'of' ci waxu 'advantage' ci ñuul solemes waxe ngir noun: 'It has many advantages' (dafa 'advantages of').

title: Narrating a story / Jottingal xisaar
bridge: Àddina wolof, ñu xisaarloo xisaaru, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi ak yeneen yi, te ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi ak ñu defarloo xisaar yi, mooy li waraloon. Àddina angale, moom lañuy jàppee ngone yi, waaye ak yeneen yi, 'past simple' la guy xisaarloo xisaar yi, 'past continuous' la guy xisaarloo xisaar yi ak yeneen yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi. Jot nañu ngone yi mooy, ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi, waaye ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi, mooy li waraloon.
rule:
Ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi àddina angale, ñu jàppee ngone yi:
1. **Past Simple** (xisaarloo xisaar yi: xisaaru + verbu xisaar yi, p. ej. 'walked'; xisaarloo xisaar yi: 'didn't + verbu'; xisaarloo xisaar yi: 'Did + xisaaru + verbu?'). Mooy li waraloon ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi.
2. **Past Continuous** (was/were + verbu xisaar yi -ing). Mooy li waraloon ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi, ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi.
3. **Past Perfect** (had + participu xisaar yi). Mooy li waraloon ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi, ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi.
4. **'Used to'** (xisaaru + used to + verbu xisaar yi) ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi.
5. **'Would'** ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi (àddina xisaaru).
Xisaarloo xisaar yi: 'first', 'then', 'after that', 'suddenly', 'finally', etc. Mooy li waraloon ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi.
Jot nañu ngone yi mooy, ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi, waaye ñu xisaarloo xisaar yi, ñu defaroon nañu ñaata ngone yi, mooy li waraloon.

title: Arguing a point of view / Wékk wax
bridge: Àddina ci Spanyol, nu ngi dégg ba waxe ci njàqare, ngi ngi ciy waxe 'bañ a dégg' 'walla bañ waxe', ngi ngi déy ba ci suuf si, waaye ci Angale, suuf si man a ngi dégg, ngi ngi ciy kàddu 'I think that...' 'walla In my opinion...'. Ngii déy ba ci Angale, ngi ngi ciy waxe 'should' ba waxe ngi dégg, waaye ci Spanyol, ngi ngi ciy waxe 'debería' 'walla tendría que'. Tégg ci yékkati, ngi déy ba ngi waxe 'yo pienso que' 'I think that' (sama wax), waaye déy ngi ba suuf si, 'Pienso que' = 'I think that' (déna 'Think that'). Yitte benn wax ji ngi déy ba ngi waxe 'I am agree' ci 'I agree', ngénn ci Spanyol 'estar de acuerdo' ngi waxe 'estar', waaye ci Angale 'agree' moom mi ngi dégg
rule:
Ci nataal B1, ngi déy ba ngi waxe njàqare ci Angale, ngi ciy kàddu:

1. **Waxe njàqare:** 'I think (that)...', 'I believe (that)...', 'In my opinion...', 'From my point of view...'. Màgg: 'I think that recycling is important.'
2. **Jëfandikoo yoon:** 'because', 'since', 'as'. Màgg: 'I believe we should save water because it's essential for life.'
3. **Defaroon ndimbal:** 'should' + verbe bu dégg (déna 'to'). Màgg: 'People should use public transport more.'
4. **Waxe njàqare / déggante:** 'I agree', 'I disagree', 'I agree with you', 'I don't agree'. Tégg: 'agree' mi ngi dégg, déna adjektif, ngénn ngi déy ba ngi waxe 'be + agree'. Màgg: 'I agree with your idea.' (Déna: 'I am agree').
5. **Dagge:** 'However', 'but', 'on the other hand'. Màgg: 'Some people think that, but I disagree.'

Tégg ci yékkati, ci Angale suuf si déy ngi dégg, ndax ngi déy ba ngi waxe 'I agree' déna 'Agree'. Ngii déy ba ngi waxe 'think' 'walla 'believe' ngi ciy kàddu 'that' (déna wax) 'walla déy ngi ba njàqare. Ci B1, ngi déy ba ngi waxe 'that' ba waxe njàqare. Adjectif yi ngi déy ba ngi waxe 'be' (I am sure), waaye verbe yi déy ngi dégg 'be'.

title: Talking about your job and career / Waxtu waxe ak jaayngal yi
bridge: Ñu ngi ci Wolof, ñu xam ne ko defar verbe 'wax' ak 'de' (waxe de doktoor), waaye ñatti ngi ci Angale, ñu xam ne ko defar verbe 'work as' (I work as a doctor) walla 'be' (I am a doctor). Ginnaaw, Angale yi def ko waxtu waxe ak jaayngal yi, waaye Wolof, ñu xam ne ko waxe 'wax' ak 'jaayngal' ci bopp.
rule:
Waxtu waxe ak jaayngal yi ñatti ngi ci Angale, ñu xam ne ko def:
- Present simple ñu defar waxe jaayngal yi: 'I work as a teacher' (waxe de profesor) walla 'I am a teacher'.
- 'Work in' + sektor walla ndaw, 'work for' + kumpaani, 'work with' + nit walla yëngu-yëngu. 
- Waxtu waxe ak jaayngal yi, ñu xam ne ko defar 'career' (jaayngal) ak 'job' (jaayngal gu mag).
- Waxtu waxe ak jaayngal yi, ñu xam ne ko defar 'would like to' + infinitif (I'd like to change careers) walla 'planning to' (I'm planning to look for a new job).
- Ñu xam ne ko defar adverbe yi: 'always', 'usually', 'often', 'sometimes', 'never' waxtu waxe ak jaayngal yi.

title: Describing processes / Jëmbéelul yàq
bridge: Àdduna, ñu jëmbéelul yàq bokk ci wàllug voz pasiva ngir 'se' (baat ba, 'se calienta el agua') bee ngir présent simple. Ànglès, mooy ki ngi bokk ci wàllug voz pasiva ngir 'is/are + participio' (baat ba, 'the water is heated') ak séquenceur ci 'first', 'then', 'next', 'after that', 'finally'. Yàqal gu mag ci man, àdduna, ñu jëmbéelul yàq, ñu defaroonal sujets, màg ànglès, voz pasiva def naan ko, bee ngir wàllug 'you' bee 'they'. Wàllug ànglès, mooy ki ngi bokk ci wàllug sujets, wàllug verbe, ak adverbe de fréquence ngi def ànd ak verbe principal, màg 'be'.
rule: Jëmbéelul yàq ànglès, level B1, mooy ki ngi bokk ci présent simple (baat ba, yàq gu mag gu yàq) ak voz pasiva (present passive: am/is/are + past participle) làkk, yàq gu mag gu yàq, màg gu yàq gu def. Struktiir gu yàq, mooy: First, [object] is/are + past participle. Luego, ñu defaroonal séquenceur: first, then, next, after that, later, finally. Ñu defaroonal bee ngir imperatif (baat ba, ànglès ci instruksiyong) bee 'you' impersonal. Voz pasiva, mooy ki ngi def: sujets + verbe 'to be' conjugé + participio passé. Baat ba, 'The coffee is ground.' Dégg na, adverbe de fréquence (always, usually, often) def ànd ak verbe principal, màg 'be' (baat ba, 'The water is always heated first'). Ànglès, àdduna, ñu defaroonal 'se' ci voz pasiva; ñu defaroonal voz pasiva ngir 'be' bee ngir wàllug 'you'.

title: Expressing uncertainty and possibility / Waxtañu xelmu ak xelmu yi
bridge: Ci waxu ñu waxe wolof, ñu defaroon lu ñu xeloon xelmu, ndaxtey adverb yi ak 'moom' ak 'baax na', waaye ci angiis ñu def ko, ñu xam ne modaal yi ak adverb yi ak 'maybe' ak 'perhaps'. Bal ma: 'must' moom kay 'dey' bu xelmu, waaye lu bokk ci ñu def deduktiyon wu nguur (dey dey)
rule: Waxtañu xelmu ci angiis, ñu def: 1) Adverb: 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'probably', 'definitely' (ci taw ba ci suuf si). 2) Modaal: 'may', 'might', 'could' ci posibilite (may/might yi ñu amul, could yi ñu amul ci affirmative). 3) 'Must' ci deduktiyon logique: 'She must be at home'. 4) Konjugasyon 'be likely to' ak 'be unlikely to' ci probabilité. Ci negatif, ñu def 'might not' ak 'may not' (dégg na 'could not' ci posibilite, waaye 'couldn't' moom kay defaroon habilite passé)

title: Making formal requests / Peticiones formales ak escritura formal básica
bridge: En español, a menudo usamos el condicional ('¿Podría...?', '¿Sería posible...?') para peticions formales. En inglés, además del condicional, es muy común usar 'Would you mind...?' seguido de gerundio (-ing), una estructura que no tiene equivalente directo en español. Ten cuidado de no traducir literalmente '¿Te importaría...?' como 'Would you care...?', ya que suena anticuado. También recuerda que en inglés formal, 'please' suele ir al final o después del verbo modal, no al principio como en español.
rule:
Para hacer peticions formales en inglés (nivel B1), usa las siguientes estructuras:
1. **Would you + verbo base...?** – 'Would you send me the report?' (¿Podría enviarme el informe?). Es educado y común.
2. **Could you + verbo base...?** – 'Could you help me with this?' (¿Podría ayudarme con esto?). Similar a 'Would', pero ligeramente menos formal.
3. **Would you mind + gerundio (-ing)?** – 'Would you mind closing the window?' (¿Le importaría cerrar la ventana?). Esta estructura es muy educada y se usa para acciones que pueden molestar. Responde 'No, not at all' si no te importa.
4. **I would like to + verbo base** – 'I would like to request a refund.' (Me gustaría solicitar un reembolso). Para expresar tu propia petición.
5. **Formal questions con 'Would it be possible to...?'** – 'Would it be possible to reschedule the meeting?' (¿Sería posible reprogramar la reunión?). Muy formal, usado en correos.
Recuerda: en inglés, el 'please' se coloca al final de la frase o después del sujeto en preguntas, no al comienzo como en español. Ej.: 'Could you help me, please?' no 'Please, could you help me?'.
